findings.english_quote: Some were dry but not worm-eaten
findings.issue: The selected source describes these rods as uneaten, without restricting the negation to damage by worms. “Not worm-eaten” narrows that assertion: it does not exclude their having been eaten in another way. The preceding worm imagery supplies context but should not reduce the scope of this negative description.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed replacement for fresh review: “Some were dry but had not been eaten.”

summary: Both editions were reviewed clause by clause against the supplied working Greek. The standard edition is acceptable; the simplified edition needs a small correction to preserve the unrestricted negation in section 6. The standard’s bracketed “rods” supplies an understood noun rather than purporting to reproduce an explicit noun at those locations. No alternative readings or manuscript reports were supplied, and this review does not certify unseen witnesses or editions.
